thread:
anya: heads-up — p99 jumped ~35% on the canary group after last night’s runtime change. seeing a lot of longprompt + tool-call tails. attaching initial logs below.

deploy-bot: deployed commit c7f3a4d to canary (runtime: kernel-picker v2.9.1). 6 nodes, 10% traffic.

sam: thanks, anya. quick question — is the spike correlated with sequence length distribution or toolcall rate?

anya: short check: median seq len ~220, p95 ~800 for this workload. tool-call fraction up 3x on canary (we route more legacy tool chains there).

mike: ran a perf trace on a affected request. flamegraph: https://internal-traces/fg/222333 — main hotspot in kernel_select_path() and then in toolcall reentry handler.

liz: can we bisect to kernel-picker change? simple A/B: v2.9.0 (baseline) vs v2.9.1 (canary).

sam: already did local bisection on a replay subset. hypothesis: kernel policy started preferring "small-batch-optimized" kernels for spiky sequences which reduces throughput for long tool-call sessions due to KV cache thrash.

anya: that matches logs: we see repeated KV cache rehashes and increased cache misses when toolcalls cause reentrant decode loops. snippet: 
```
KVCacheStats { hits: 123, misses: 987, evictions: 45 }
reentrant_calls: 7
avg_microbatch_size: 1.2
```

mike: note from perf: when reentry happens, we end up flushing microbatch boundaries, switching kernel variant mid-request, and that creates extra memcpy + kernel setup cost ~5-8ms per switch. p99 accumulates.

sam: nailed it down to two things in v2.9.1: (1) kernel_picker now biases toward kernels optimized for short context (less register tiling) when batch_size<4, (2) changed batching heuristic to prefer lower latency (smaller microbatches) under load spikes. both are fine independently but combined they hurt reentrant tool loops.

anya: payload example that reproduces: long system prompt + user prompt triggers toolcall, tool returns JSON (large), generator reenters with long added context. microbatch goes 3->1 and kernel switches.

liz: action items?

sam: propose immediate canary rollback of kernel-picker to v2.9.0 while we fix heuristics. also add a gate: if request.reentrant_toolcall_count > 0 prefer stable kernel family (avoid small-batch specialized kernels).

mike: agree. quick patch to gating logic looks like: 
```
if (req.reentrant_toolcall_count > 0 || seq_len > 1024) {
  kernel_policy = prefer_stable_kernels;
} else if (predicted_batch_size < 4) {
  kernel_policy = latency_opt_smallbatch;
}
```

anya: can we also tweak microbatch sizing to avoid immediate downscaling to 1 during reentry? maybe min_microbatch_on_reentry = 2?

sam: yes. heuristic: keep microbatch >= max(2, floor(predicted_batch_size/2)) when reentry detected and latency SLO allows p95 headroom. that reduces kernel flip frequency.

trace-bot: trace 222333-A created: traces attached for 12 failing canary requests.

liz: we should add a short unit/integration test in the replay harness: synthetic toolcall that returns 3-6k tokens mid-gen and assert no kernel_switches > 1. canary test added to CI.

mike: performance diff numbers from replay: baseline v2.9.0 p99=98ms, v2.9.1 p99=132ms (35% reg). after gating patch locally p99=105ms. still some overhead but much better.

anya: rolling back canary now. deploy-bot: rollback c7f3a4d -> v2.9.0 on canary.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated, expected 2-3 minutes.

sam: follow-up longer-term: evaluate kernel families on a matrix: (seq_len buckets) x (microbatch size) x (reentrant flag) x (toolcall payload size). maybe auto-tune policy per-model. also consider warm-KV prefetch on tool-return to avoid cold misses.

liz: add monitoring alert: if p99 increases >20% on canary and toolcall_fraction > 2x baseline, auto-gate kernel_picker and scale microbatch upwards for affected route.

anya: thanks all. documenting steps in the perf runbook and will upload traces + replay shard to the incident board. :thumbsup:

mike: note — we should also consider lightweight kernel hot-paths that avoid recompile when batch size oscillates by checking compatibility matrix cheaply. small wins.

sam: agreed. i'll open RFC with data and a small prototyped gating patch. putting follow-up on eng-runtime sync.

anya: closing thread for now; reopen if rollback doesn't restore p99 within 10m.

liz: re: postmortem, include regression testcase, bisection notes, and the minimal patch that fixed the canary replay (sam's gating change).
